question: Which of the following animals have more neck (cervical) vertebrae than many other animals?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Birds.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Birds** have more neck (cervical) vertebrae than many other animals, typically ranging from 13 to 25. This high number of cervical vertebrae in birds allows for greater flexibility in their neck movements, which is essential for various activities such as grooming their feathers and capturing prey. 
 
• **Giraffes** typically have 7 cervical vertebrae, just like most mammals, including humans. This number is relatively low compared to birds but contributes to their exceptionally long necks, as each cervical vertebra is elongated.
 
• In tetrapods, **cervical vertebrae** are the vertebrae of the **neck, immediately below the skull.**
 
• Truncal vertebrae (divided into thoracic and lumbar vertebrae in mammals) lie **caudal (toward the tail) of cervical vertebrae.**
 
• In sauropsid species, the cervical vertebrae **bear cervical ribs.**
 
• In lizards and saurischian dinosaurs, the cervical** ribs are large; in birds, they are small and completely fused **__to the vertebrae.
 
• The vertebral** transverse processes of mammals **are homologous to the cervical ribs of other amniotes.
 
• Most mammals have seven** cervical vertebrae,** with the only three known exceptions being the manatee with six, the two-toed sloth with five or six, and the three-toed sloth with nine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** **Taxonomy**

__
 
• In the **classification of animals**, some animals are widely** similar in behaviors, eating habits,** features, and habitat choice, while others are poles apart and chose to** behave totally differently.**
 
• The reason for this is simple, as these** animals are classified into various categories** based on their similarities.
 
• All living beings were divided into two groups by** Aristotle - animal group and plant group.**
 
• In his **book Systema Naturae,**__ Linnaeus divided all living beings into **two kingdoms, the plant kingdom and the animal kingdom.**
 
• Linnaeus is called the** father of modern taxonomy.**

** Five-Kingdom Classification of Organism**

 
• The traditional Two-kingdom classification was eventually **replaced by the Five-kingdom **system proposed by **Whittaker in 1969.**
 
• According to this all living beings are classified into the** following five kingdoms.**
 
 
• **Monera, Protista, Plantae, Fungi, Animal**
